{{short description|Hungarian-Canadian mathematician}}
'''George A. Grätzer''' ({{langx|hu|Grätzer György}}; born 2 August 1936, in [[Budapest]]) is a Hungarian-Canadian mathematician, specializing in [[lattice theory]] and [[universal algebra]]. He is known for his books on [[LaTeX]]<ref>[http://tug.org/interviews/gratzer.html Interview with George Grätzer – TeX Users Group, 2005]</ref> and his proof with E. Tamás Schmidt of the Grätzer–Schmidt theorem.<ref>[http://www.latticetheory.net/media/pdf/Gratzer_and_Schmidt_Bio.pdf "G. Grätzer and E. T. Schmidt, mathematicians" by Gábor Czédli]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Fuchs, Lászlo|title=Reminiscences about George Grätzer and E. Tamás Schmidt|journal=Algebra Universalis|year=2008|volume=59 |issue=1–2 |pages=1–10 |doi=10.1007/s00012-008-2129-2|s2cid=116832764 }}</ref>

==Biography==
His father József Grätzer was famous in Hungary as the "Puzzle King" ("rejtvénykirály"). George Grätzer received his PhD from [[Eötvös Loránd University]] in 1960 under the supervision of [[László Fuchs]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=24938}}</ref> In 1963 Grätzer and Schmidt published their theorem on the characterization of [[congruence lattice]]s of algebras.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Czédli, Gábor|title=The mathematics of G. Grätzer and E. T. Schmidt|journal=Algebra Universalis|year=2008|volume=59 |issue=1–2 |pages=11–30 |doi=10.1007/s00012-008-2130-9|s2cid=121478085 }}</ref> In 1963 Grätzer left Hungary and became a professor at [[Pennsylvania State University]]. In 1966 he became a professor at the [[University of Manitoba]] and later a Canadian citizen. In 1970 Grätzer became the founder and editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Algebra Universalis]]''. His mathematical articles—over 260, all listed on [[ResearchGate|Research Gate]]—are widely cited, and he has written several influential books.

Grätzer has received several awards and honours. He is married and has two children (Tom Gratzer and [[David Gratzer]]) and five grandchildren.

==Awards and honours==
* Grünwald Memorial Prize (1967)
* [[Steacie Prize]] (1971)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.steacieprize.ca/recipients_e.html |title=The Steacie Prize – Recipients |access-date=2014-04-10 |archive-date=2021-06-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602232712/http://www.steacieprize.ca/recipients_e.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] (1973)
* [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]] (1978)
* Zubek Prize (1987)
* Elected Foreign Member of [[Magyar Tudományos Akadémia]] (1997)

==Publications==

More than 270 research articles in mathematics, and 36 books including

* ''Elmesport egy esztendőre'' 1959 (2008-as kiadása: {{ISBN|9789639725362}}); trans. into English as [https://books.google.com/books/about/Train_Your_Brain.html?id=6kJ-Es86orUC ''Train your brain: A year's worth of puzzles''] 2011
* ''Universal Algebra'' 1967
* ''Lattice Theory'' 1971
* ''General Lattice Theory'' 1978
* [[VP-Info]]''VP-Info Database Language'' 1986
* [https://books.google.com/books/about/First_Steps_in_LaTeX.html?id=mLdg5ZdDKToC ''First Steps in LaTeX''] 1999
* [https://books.google.com/books/about/More_Math_Into_LaTeX.html?id=6WTZ0Rpiwp8C ''More Math into LaTeX''], sixth edition 2007
* ''Lattice Theory: Foundation'' 2011
* ''Practical LaTeX'' 2014
* ''The Congruences of a Finite Lattice: A Proof-by-Picture Approach, third edition'' 2023
* ''Math into LaTeX, sixth edition'' 2024
* ''Math into English,'' 2024
* ''Write Better,'' 2024
